walkthrough:
Use the arc length formula $s = r\theta$ with arc length $s = 4\text{ cm}$ and radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$\angle BAC = \theta = \frac{s}{r} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8\text{ radians}$$

hints: Calculate trapezium area $\approx 11.69\text{ cm}^2$ and sector area $10\text{ cm}^2$.
Subtract to find shaded area $\approx 1.69\text{ cm}^2$.
walkthrough:
In the coordinate system with $A$ at $(0, 0)$ and $B$ along the axis at $(5, 0)$:
$$BD = 5\sin(0.8) \approx 5(0.717356) \approx 3.5868\text{ cm}$$
$$DC = 5 - 5\cos(0.8) \approx 5 - 5(0.696707) \approx 5 - 3.4835 = 1.5165\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of right-trapezium $ABDC$ (with parallel sides $AB = 5\text{ cm}$ and $DC \approx 1.5165\text{ cm}$ and height $BD \approx 3.5868\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Area}(ABDC) = \frac{1}{2}(AB + DC)(BD) = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 1.5165)(3.5868) = \frac{1}{2}(6.5165)(3.5868) \approx 11.6860\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of sector $ABC$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)(0.8) = 10\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the trapezium area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}(ABDC) - \text{Area}(\text{sector } ABC) = 11.6860 - 10 = 1.6860 \approx 1.69\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$
